masonry_surface_input_group.description: Rate per SF applies to net masonry wall field area from PaintScope. Engine divides SF by rate to calculate hours.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. ~30 sec per LF. Includes staking and securing tarps at grade line. LF-based. Identical rate to engineered wood and fiber cement siblings.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Coverage adequate along working elevation. Minor gaps acceptable if no spray overspray risk.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full perimeter coverage of plantings within spray drift zone (10-15 ft). Secure against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete perimeter coverage secured at all edges. No gaps in protection.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on flat walkway and patio surfaces. ~14 sec per SF. Covers both hardscape_walk and hardscape_patio zones. Identical rate to sibling specs.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key areas covered. Minor gaps acceptable away from spray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of walkways and patios within overspray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Non-slip canvas on crew traffic areas.

task_production_rates.name: Fixture and Utility Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Bag and tape light fixtures and HVAC units with plastic and blue tape (smooth fixture surfaces). ~5 min per fixture average. HVAC units take longer (~10-12 min). Slightly slower than siding spec (15 EA/hr) because masonry-adjacent fixtures often require stucco tape transition from masonry surface to fixture bag.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Fixtures bagged. Tape coverage adequate.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. All fixtures and utilities fully masked.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage with clean tape lines. Cover plates removed where accessible.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Configure airless sprayer: install correct tip (517 for acrylic/primer, 531 for block filler/elastomeric), install correct filter (60-mesh or 30-mesh), run lines, test pattern, stage roller frames and thick-nap covers for back-rolling. ~55 min. Slightly longer than siding (50 min) due to potential tip/filter changes between block filler and acrylic products. Per elevation.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment functional. Tip pattern acceptable.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern on cardboard. Correct tip and filter for product. Roller covers staged for back-rolling.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern verified at correct distance. Backup tips staged. Fresh roller covers for back-rolling.

task_production_rates.name: Brush/Roll Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stage thick-nap roller covers (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch), roller frames, extension poles, trays, brushes, access equipment. ~20 min. Per elevation. Same as siding spec.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment staged and functional.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Fresh thick-nap roller covers. Brushes in good condition.
defect_tolerance.QT4: New thick-nap roller covers. Premium brushes. Materials pre-mixed.

task_production_rates.name: Cure Time Verification
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Review construction schedule for pour/lay date, calculate cure days (28-day standard, 7-day accelerated with alkali-resistant primer), document in project file. ~15 min fixed time. Administrative/verification task — not area-dependent.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Verify cure date from GC. Document.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Verify cure date from GC. Document in project file. Confirm accelerated path eligibility.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Verify cure date with documentation. Confirm accelerated path eligibility. Photograph date stamp if available.

task_production_rates.name: Moisture Content Testing

QT2.notes: Spot check representative areas on each elevation. Quick pin-meter readings at 3-4 points per elevation.

QT3.notes: Multiple test points per elevation. Document readings. Test at ground level, mid-height, and near grade.

QT4.notes: Systematic grid pattern. All readings documented with location map. Every area must pass <12% MC.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pin-type moisture meter checks across masonry wall surfaces. MC >12% is HARD STOP. QT2 spot checks only (~1.8 sec/SF average), QT3 systematic sampling (~3 sec/SF), QT4 full documentation grid (~6 sec/SF). Masonry-specific — more thorough than siding moisture checks because masonry retains moisture longer.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Spot check representative areas. Surface reads <12% MC.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Check multiple points per elevation. All readings <12% MC. Documented.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic grid check. All readings documented with location. All areas <12% MC.

task_production_rates.name: Efflorescence Treatment

QT2.notes: Brush off loose efflorescence. Water wash. Minimal treatment.

QT3.notes: Full removal with stiff brush and TSP if moderate. Rinse. Verify no recurrence.

QT4.notes: Complete removal. TSP or acid wash as required. Document treatment. Verify no recurrence before coating.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Efflorescence treatment by stiff brush + water (light), TSP solution (moderate), or acid wash (severe). Rates based on research range 200-400 SF/hr. QT4 slower due to documentation and full chemical treatment cycle (pre-dampen, scrub, neutralize, rinse). Site-condition driven: include_when efflorescence_present. No acid on limestone.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Loose efflorescence removed. No active white deposits on surface.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full removal. No visible efflorescence. Moisture source question addressed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete removal verified. Treatment documented. Moisture source investigation complete.

task_production_rates.name: Power Wash Masonry Surface

QT2.notes: Basic power wash to remove visible dirt and debris. 1,500 PSI.

QT3.notes: Full power wash with detergent. Rinse thoroughly. 2,000 PSI.

QT4.notes: Full power wash with TSP solution. Rinse thoroughly. 2,500 PSI max.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Power wash IS allowed on masonry (unlike fiber cement/engineered wood). Research range 800-1200 SF/hr. Masonry tolerates 1,500-2,500 PSI without damage. QT4 slower due to TSP pre-treatment and more thorough rinse. 24-48 hr dry time before coating (not included in rate).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible dirt and debris removed. Surface appears clean.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All construction dust, dirt, and debris removed. Allow 24-48 hr dry time.
defect_tolerance.QT4: TSP solution wash. Pristine surface. Allow 48 hr dry time. Moisture meter check mandatory after drying.

task_production_rates.name: Form-Release Agent Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove form-release agents and curing compounds from cast concrete by abrasive pad, chemical detergent, or abrasive blasting. ~24 sec per SF. Concrete substrate ONLY. Water bead test to verify removal completeness. Labor-intensive task — these are bond-breakers that resist removal.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Form-release removed from coating areas. Water bead test passes on representative spots.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full removal. Water bead test passes on all areas. Surface absorbs water uniformly.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full removal verified. Water bead test passes everywhere. Document before/after.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Masonry-to-Trim Joints

QT3.notes: All masonry-to-trim joints. Smooth tool. Clean edges.

QT4.notes: All joints. Precision tool smooth. Mask both sides (stucco tape on masonry, blue tape on trim).

task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Linear feet of masonry-to-trim joints (window casings, door casings, soffit transitions). Not auto-captured by PaintScope — estimator enters count from field measure.
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply and tool polyurethane exterior caulk at masonry-to-trim joints. QT4 is slower due to double-masking (stucco tape on masonry side + blue tape on trim side) and precision tooling. Similar to siding caulk (90 LF/hr) but masonry joints require stucco tape which adds time.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key joints caulked. Basic bead. No voids.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All joints caulked. Smooth tool. Clean edges. No excess.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth. Uniform appearance.

task_production_rates.name: Surface Defect Repair

QT3.notes: Repair obvious defects and cracked mortar joints.

QT4.notes: Repair all defects. Fill bug holes in concrete. Match surrounding texture.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Patch spalled mortar, cracked joints, bug holes with masonry patching compound or hydraulic cement. Rate is per total wall SF (most of the wall passes without repair — rate reflects scan + spot repair). QT3 fixes obvious only, QT4 repairs all defects. QT2 excluded (no repair at economy tier). QT4 is very slow because all bug holes and hairline cracks must be addressed.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects and cracked mortar repaired. No structural cracks left unpatched.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired. Bug holes filled on concrete. Patches blended to match surrounding texture.

task_production_rates.name: Block Filler - Spray + Back-Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray (527-535 tip, 30-mesh filter, 2,300-3,000 PSI) followed immediately by back-rolling with 1-1/2 inch nap roller. Research range 200-350 SF/hr but block filler is the heaviest-body product — very thick material, slow application. 150 SF/hr per crew-hour reflects 2-person operation (sprayer + roller). Spray/backroll coupling: spray rate (150) <= backroll rate (150) -- compliant. Single coat. CMU only.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Voids filled to PCA P12 Level 2 standard. No unfilled voids visible.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All voids filled. Roller distributes filler into every void. Max 10 voids per SF after application.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All voids filled. Roller passes verified. PCA P12 Level 2 fully achieved.

task_production_rates.name: Block Filler - Heavy Roller Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Heavy roller (1-1/2 inch nap) application of block filler. Fallback method for smaller CMU areas. Multiple passes needed to force thick filler into voids. ~45 sec per SF. Very slow — heavy-body material does not flow off roller easily. Single coat. CMU only.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Voids filled. Multiple passes if needed.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All voids filled. Heavy pressure. PCA P12 Level 2 verified.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All voids filled. PCA P12 Level 2. Inspect every section.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer - Spray + Back-Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray (517 tip, 60-mesh filter, 1,500-2,500 PSI) followed immediately by back-rolling with 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap. Research range 350-500 SF/hr for primer spray_backroll — 200 SF/hr per crew-hour for 2-person operation is midpoint of 160-250 range. Back-rolling forces alkali-resistant primer into porous masonry for continuous protective film. Spray/backroll coupling: spray rate (200) <= backroll rate (200) -- compliant. Single coat. Mandatory on ALL new masonry.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots. Back-roll immediately.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. Back-roll within 30-60 seconds of spray. Full pore saturation.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Every pore saturated. Inspect under raking light on primary elevations.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Heavy roller (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap) application of alkali-resistant primer. ~29 sec per SF. Research range 150-400 SF/hr for roll primer on masonry — 125 SF/hr reflects heavy-nap roller on porous substrate requiring heavy pressure. Excellent mechanical bond. Single coat.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Primer worked into all pores and mortar joints.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage. Heavy nap saturates all texture. No thin spots.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer - Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush application of primer on masonry. Detail work and small areas only — brush is never primary method for masonry wall field. ~55 sec per SF. Research range 50-100 SF/hr for brush on masonry. Must work primer into mortar joints and surface texture by hand.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Primer worked into mortar joints.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage. All mortar joints and surface texture saturated.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full coverage. Every pore and mortar joint. Maintain wet edge.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 - Spray + Back-Roll (Acrylic)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray + immediate back-roll for acrylic finish on primed masonry. Research range 400-600 SF/hr for spray_backroll finish — 225 SF/hr per crew-hour (2-person) is conservative midpoint accounting for masonry texture and mortar joints. Spray/backroll coupling: spray rate (225) <= backroll rate (225) -- compliant. For ELASTOMERIC coating_system: apply FAC_MSRY_COATING_SYSTEM modifier (1.50x) which reduces effective rate to 150 SF/hr — aligning with research 150-250 SF/hr range for elastomeric.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Back-roll within 30-60 seconds. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. Consistent roller texture. No dry spots in mortar joints.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Every mortar joint and surface irregularity fully coated. Raking light check on visible elevations.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Heavy roller (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap) application of acrylic finish on primed masonry. ~24 sec per SF. Research range 150-400 SF/hr for roll finish — 150 SF/hr is conservative for textured masonry. For ELASTOMERIC: apply FAC_MSRY_COATING_SYSTEM modifier (1.50x) reducing to 100 SF/hr — elastomeric is dramatically thicker and slower to roll.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Consistent roller texture. All mortar joints covered. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform appearance. Heavy nap saturates all texture. No lap marks.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 - Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush application of finish on masonry. Detail work and small areas. ~51 sec per SF. Research range 50-100 SF/hr for brush finish on masonry. Must work finish into mortar joints.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Finish worked into mortar joints.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage. All joints. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full coverage. Every pore and joint. Even appearance.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Inspection

QT3.notes: Ground-level walkthrough. Check all elevations for holidays, runs, missed mortar joints. Quick scan.

QT4.notes: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Raking light on visible elevations. Mark all defects. Check mortar joints for complete coverage.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection of first finish coat. Masonry-specific: check mortar joints, pinholes (incomplete backroll), and surface irregularity coverage. Same tier-based rates as siding sibling. QT3 quick scan, QT4 systematic with raking light and marking.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Note obvious runs, sags, holidays, and missed mortar joints. Quick visual scan.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic scan. All visible defects marked. Raking light check on primary elevations.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Light Sand (QT4 Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 220 grit light sand on anomalies only — do NOT attempt to sand entire textured masonry surface. ~14 sec per SF. Slightly slower than siding (300 SF/hr) because masonry texture makes sanding more difficult and sanding block cannot achieve flat contact. Tack cloth dust removal included.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Anomalies sanded smooth. Nibs and defects removed. No deep scratches. Tack cloth dust removal complete.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Touch-Up

QT3.notes: Fix obvious defects — holidays, missed mortar joints. Minimal touch-up.

QT4.notes: Fix all found defects. Blend repairs into surrounding finish. Focus on mortar joints and coverage gaps.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during interstage inspection. Rate is per total wall SF — most area passes without touch-up. QT3 minimal, QT4 thorough with blending. Same rates as siding sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects repaired. No visible holidays or missed joints remain.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired and blended. Repairs invisible at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 - Spray + Back-Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 spray_backroll. Primed and first-coated surface provides more consistent absorption than bare masonry. Two-person operation. For ELASTOMERIC: apply FAC_MSRY_COATING_SYSTEM modifier (1.50x) reducing to 150 SF/hr. Final appearance coat. Spray/backroll coupling compliant.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. No visible pattern at 6 ft.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat. For elastomeric: verify DFT target 20-30 mils cumulative.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 roll. Sealed surface allows consistent production. For ELASTOMERIC: apply FAC_MSRY_COATING_SYSTEM modifier (1.50x) reducing to 100 SF/hr. Final coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent roller texture. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform appearance. No lap marks. Final coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 - Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 brush. Detail work. Final coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Even coverage. Every joint and pore. Final coat.

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection

QT2.notes: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for obvious misses.

QT3.notes: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Backlight check (late afternoon sun angle) on primary elevation.

QT4.notes: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard. Raking light and backlight check on all visible elevations.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final walkthrough of all elevations. Masonry-specific: check mortar joints and surface irregularities for holidays using backlighting (sun angle). Same rates as siding sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: No obvious misses or holidays visible from ground.
defect_tolerance.QT3: No defects visible at 6-10 ft from ground level. Backlight passes.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No defects visible at 6 ft with binoculars. Coverage uniform across all elevations.

task_production_rates.name: Final Touch-Up

QT2.notes: Minimal touch-up. Fix obvious misses only.

QT3.notes: Fix all noted defects. Focus on mortar joints and holidays.

QT4.notes: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly. Focus on mortar joint coverage and surface uniformity.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Rate is per total wall SF. Same rates as siding sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Obvious misses touched up.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All noted defects repaired.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended seamlessly.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all stucco tape, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, HVAC covers, and plastic sheeting along perimeter. ~18 sec per LF. Faster than setup. Check for stucco tape adhesive residue — stucco tape can leave residue if overexposed to UV. Same rate as siding sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All protection materials removed.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All materials removed. No tape residue on surfaces. Check landscape for overspray.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All materials removed. Check for tape residue. Inspect for any paint on protected surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Equipment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Flush airless sprayer (full flush cycle — masonry coatings are abrasive and block filler/elastomeric require thorough flushing). Clean tips and filters. Inspect tips for wear (cementitious substrates cause accelerated wear). Clean roller frames, dispose of saturated thick-nap covers. ~40 min per session. Longer than siding (35 min) due to heavy-body materials requiring more thorough flushing.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment flushed and stored.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full flush. Tips and filters cleaned. Tip wear inspected. Roller covers disposed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full flush cycle. Tips and filters cleaned and inspected. Equipment ready for next use.

task_production_rates.name: Site Debris Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Collect all debris — caulk tubes, stucco tape, plastic sheeting, paint cans, block filler containers, used thick-nap roller covers, brush containers. Dispose properly. Final site walkthrough. ~20 min. Same as siding sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All debris collected and disposed.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials removed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Site restored. Walkthrough with customer. No evidence of work activity.

factor_modifiers.name: Access Type Height Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Access type drives production rate reduction for elevated work. Applied per elevation. Ground tasks (equipment setup, site cleanup) are not affected.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied per elevation. Protection setup/teardown, equipment setup, and site cleanup are ground-level tasks — not affected. Cure verification is administrative — not affected.

factor_modifiers.name: Masonry Substrate Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Substrate type affects production rate due to porosity, texture, and surface characteristics. Brick_smooth is baseline. Rough brick and CMU are slower (porous, textured). Concrete is faster (smooth formed surface). Limestone is slower (porous, requires care).
factor_modifiers.notes: Brick_smooth is baseline (dense, relatively smooth). Brick_rough is 30% slower (deep mortar joints, irregular surface, textured face). CMU is 20% slower (porous surface, voids slow roller). Concrete is 10% faster (smooth formed surface, consistent). Limestone is 10% slower (porous sedimentary stone, acid sensitivity requires careful cleaning). Resolution.json proposed brick=1.00/CMU=1.15/concrete=0.95/limestone=1.10 — adjusted brick to split smooth/rough because rough brick is significantly different from smooth brick.

factor_modifiers.name: Coating System Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Elastomeric coatings are dramatically thicker (20-30 mils DFT vs 6-8 mils acrylic) and require heavier application for proper film build. This slows production rate by 50%.
factor_modifiers.notes: Acrylic is baseline. Elastomeric is 50% slower due to: (1) heavier body material flows slower, (2) thicker wet film requires more passes, (3) 527-535 spray tips with heavy material, (4) back-roller must distribute dramatically more material per SF. Research range for elastomeric spray_backroll: 150-250 SF/hr — at 1.50x modifier on 225 base = 150 SF/hr effective, aligns with research low end.

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier affects overall production pace for tasks that are not already qt_scaled. QT2 is faster (economy pace), QT4 is slower (premium scrutiny). Applied to binary tasks only — qt_scaled tasks already have tier-specific rates.
factor_modifiers.notes: QT2 is 15% faster (economy pace, less scrutiny, fewer passes). QT3 is baseline. QT4 is 20% slower (premium scrutiny, careful application). Applied to binary tasks only — qt_scaled and qt_conditional tasks already encode tier differences in qt_rates. Protection tasks at QT2 can be slightly less thorough = faster.

factor_modifiers.name: Wind Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wind affects spray operations (overspray drift, pattern disruption) and general exterior work pace. High wind blocks spray entirely (SOP exclude_when). Moderate wind slows all work.
factor_modifiers.notes: High wind BLOCKS spray operations per SOP site_condition_rules. Moderate wind (5-10 mph) slows spray 15% due to pattern disruption and repositioning. Roll and brush operations are not significantly affected by wind — modifier applies to spray tasks only.

factor_modifiers.name: Sun Exposure Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Full sun exposure on masonry surfaces can cause flash drying of coatings (especially water-based acrylic and elastomeric). Forces early morning start and may reduce daily working hours.
factor_modifiers.notes: Full sun on masonry causes rapid surface heating — dark masonry can exceed 120F in direct sun. Flash drying causes lap marks, poor leveling, and reduced film build. Modifier reflects slower pace to maintain wet edge and may force elevation sequencing (shaded elevations first).

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Temperature Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Extreme surface temperatures affect coating application. Cold surfaces (<50F) extend recoat intervals. Hot surfaces (>90F) cause flash drying.
factor_modifiers.notes: Optimal: 50-90F surface temp. Cold surface (<50F): coatings cure slower, recoat windows extend, productivity drops 10%. Hot surface (>90F): BLOCKED per SOP site_condition_rules — coating fails to level before skinning. Masonry retains heat longer than wood — surface temp can exceed air temp significantly.

quality_effects.notes: Economy tier. Single finish coat of acrylic on primed surface. No interstage module. Block filler still required on CMU (not quality-optional). Elastomeric NOT available at QT2.
Standard tier. Two finish coats (acrylic or elastomeric). Interstage inspection and touch-up. No interstage sanding. Both coating systems available.
Premium tier. Two finish coats with premium products. Interstage sand if anomalies detected (QT4 only). Systematic raking light and backlight inspection. Both coating systems available.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Smooth brick, acrylic, ground access, QT3 baseline (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case — fastest finish production per 2-person crew-hour.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Smooth brick, elastomeric, ground access, QT3 (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Elastomeric on smooth brick at ground — 150 SF/hr. Aligns with research 150-250 SF/hr range for elastomeric spray_backroll.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: CMU, acrylic, scaffold access, QT4 (spray_backroll finish)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: CMU + scaffold + QT4. ~98 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Reasonable production on elevated CMU.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Rough brick, elastomeric, scaffold access, QT4 — worst case (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Worst case — near 4.0x stacking cap (3.744x). ~60 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Very slow but still fixed-price viable. Rough brick + elastomeric + scaffold + QT4.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Smooth brick, acrylic, ground, QT3 — roll only
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Roll-only baseline for smooth brick acrylic. 150 SF/hr single worker. Within research range 150-400 SF/hr.
Concrete is 10% faster (smooth formed surface). Ladder access slows 35%. Net: 185 SF/hr per 2-person crew.

assumptions: Base rates for spray_backroll are per crew-hour with 2 workers (sprayer + roller). crew_size = 2.
Base rates for roll and brush are per single worker. crew_size = 1.
Spray/backroll coupling rule satisfied on all spray_backroll tasks: spray component rate <= backroll component rate (same combined rate).
Brick_smooth is the substrate type baseline (1.00x). Split from resolution's single 'brick' value because rough/tumbled brick is 30% slower.
Coating system modifier (acrylic=1.00, elastomeric=1.50) applies to FINISH tasks only — primer and block filler are the same regardless of finish coating system.
Modifier stacking is multiplicative: effective_rate = base_rate / (substrate_type x coating_system x access x QT).
Maximum combined modifier: 3.744x (rough brick + elastomeric + scaffold + QT4). Under 4.0x stacking cap.
Block filler rates are significantly slower than primer/finish because block filler is the heaviest-body product (thickest material, slowest flow).
Cure verification is FIXED time — not area-dependent. Administrative verification task.
Moisture testing is qt_scaled because QT2 spot-checks vs QT4 full grid documentation.
Environmental conditions (wind, sun, surface temp) are declared as modifiers per exterior doctrine. High wind and hot surface BLOCK spray operations per SOP exclude_when rules.
Equipment cleanup is 40 min (longer than siding 35 min) due to heavy-body block filler and elastomeric materials requiring thorough flushing.
Caulk joint rates use manual capture LF — not auto-captured by PaintScope. Estimator enters from field measure.
Surface repair task (QT3/QT4 only) rate reflects scan + spot repair across total wall SF — most area passes without repair.
risks: Rough brick + elastomeric + scaffold + QT4 is near 4.0x stacking cap (3.744x) — flag for estimator review on these combinations.

Elastomeric spray_backroll 2-person crew + 50% slower rate = dramatically higher labor cost vs acrylic. Combined with 3-4x material cost, elastomeric projects are 5-8x more expensive per SF than acrylic.
Block filler coverage is highly variable (75-125 SF/gal) depending on CMU void density — material quantity estimates for CMU may be off by 25%.
Efflorescence treatment rate assumes light-to-moderate conditions. Severe efflorescence requiring acid wash would be much slower — flag for estimator review.
Moisture testing rate at QT4 (600 SF/hr) is estimate only — no field calibration data. Full grid documentation may take longer on complex elevations.
Form-release removal on concrete is variable — some form-release agents are extremely difficult to remove and may require abrasive blasting (much slower than 150 SF/hr base rate).
Caulk joint LF is manual capture — under-counting risks unsealed joints that allow moisture intrusion behind coating.
Stucco tape adhesive residue can occur if tape is left on masonry for extended UV exposure — flag for multi-day exterior projects.
